info.title: CloudRF API
info.description: The CloudRF API enables users to model and test radio propagation for any radio, anywhere. Authenticate by passing your API key in the request header as `key`. Set up a [CloudRF.com](https://cloudrf.com/my-account) account to generate this key. All data is transferred as JSON. For detailed documentation, visit [docs.cloudrf.com](https://docs.cloudrf.com).

post.description:
This endpoint returns an omni-directional coverage plot (point-to-multipoint) as an image.
This function assumes a consistent receiver height at all locations out to fixed radius.
Speed can be improved by adjusting the resolution with the "res" parameter.
A standard request requires a transmitter, receiver, antenna and output objects. Providing a model and environment enhances accuracy.

post.description:
This endpoint returns a ground coverage plot for a satellite spot beam as an image.
The satellite is defined by its azimuth, elevation and altitude as observed from the receiver, instead of by its actual position above the earth.
The receiver position is the centre of the output area and the propagation model is an optimistic ITU-R P.525 free space model with Bullington diffraction.
For best results, this should be used with the SATCOM colour key. Only received power (dBm) units are available with this API.

post.summary: Find the best site within an area
post.description:
The best site analysis (BSA) endpoint can be used to find the best locations in a wider area for a transmitter.
It uses a GPU accelerated Monte Carlo simulation with hundreds of random locations to compare and grade radio intervisibility.
Please note that the response of a BSA calculation is not signal strength. It is a normalised heatmap, relative to the best site, with settings for a user defined transmitter.
For best results, focus onto a single feature, like a valley or a ridge, not an entire mountain range.

There are two methods to define an area of interest for a BSA caluclation:

1. Specify the `transmitter.lat` and `transmitter.lon`, along with the `output.rad` to define the circular area of interest.
2. Pass in an array of `edges`, each with a `lat` and `lon` which defines the area of interest. When using this method, you should ensure that the `transmitter.lat` and `transmitter.lon` are not set.

The response for BSA is a greyscale image.

* `1` - Irregular Terrain Model (ITM) (Longley-Rice)
* `2` - Line of Sight (LOS)
* `3` - Okumura-Hata 
* `4` - ITU-R P.1812
* `5` - SUI Microwave
* `6` - COST231-Hata
* `7` - ITU-R P.525 (Free space path loss)
* `8` - RADAR
* `9` - Ericsson 9999
* `10` - General Purpose
* `11` - Egli VHF/UHF
* `12` - HF NVIS
* `13` - HF Skywave

pe.description:
Propagation model subtype (environment):
* `1` - Conservative (Urban)
* `2` - Average (Suburban)
* `3` - Optimistic (Rural)

ked.description:
Include knife edge diffraction for enhancing models with NLOS coverage :
  * `0` - Diffraction disabled.
  * `1` - Knife-edge diffraction enabled.
  * `2` - Bullington diffraction enabled.
  * `3` - Giovanelli diffraction enabled.
  * `4` - Deygout diffraction enabled.
  * `5` - Epstein-Peterson diffraction enabled.

rel.description: Model reliability (fade margin) represented as a percentage (%).

month.description: HF Skywave only - Month of the year

hour.description: HF Skywave only - Hour of the day

sunspots_r12.description: HF Skywave only - Average international sunspot number (https://www.voacap.com/2023/understanding/choosingssn.html)

units.description:

* `f` - Define units in (imperial) feet and miles above ground level.
* `f_amsl` - Define units in (imperial) feet and miles above mean sea level.

* 10MHz has a noise floor of -104dBm
* 20MHz has a noise floor of -101dBm

txl.description: Feeder loss in dB. A long feeder has more loss. Loss varies by material and wavelength eg. LMR-400

ant.description:
Antenna pattern code:
* `0` - Allows custom options (see: `hbw`; `vbw`; `fbr`)
* `1` - Vertical dipole (omni-directional)

Any other value is the identifier of a pattern in the antenna database, eg. `39`.

azi.description:
Antenna azimuth in degrees North.
You can use more than one azimuth at a time to simulate the same antenna pointing in different directions. To do this please use a comma-separated list, for example `0,120,240` would simulate 3 antennas spaced 120 degrees apart from true North. You can enter up to a maximum of 20 azimuth values.

tlt.description: Antenna tilt in degrees below the horizon (inverted) where horizon is `0`.

hbw.description: Custom antenna horizontal beamwidth in degrees. For use only with `ant` value of `0`.

vbw.description: Custom antenna vertical beamwidth in degrees. For use only with `ant` value of `0`.

fbr.description: Front-to-back ratio measured in dB. A highly directional antenna will have a high FBR.

ked.description:
Include knife edge diffraction for enhancing models with NLOS coverage (ITM includes this already):
* `0` - Diffraction disabled. In such cases the model applies a conservative line of sight.
* `1` - Knife-edge diffraction enabled.
* `2` - Bullington diffraction enabled.
* `3` - Giovanelli diffraction enabled.
* `4` - Deygout diffraction enabled.
* `5` - Epstein-Peterson diffraction enabled.

rel.description: Model reliability (aka fade margin) represented as a percentage (%) where 50% adds 0dB loss, 99% adds 9.9dB loss.

rcs.description:
Set the RADAR cross section to indicate the reflective surface of an object. 

This value is taken in square meters (m<sup>2</sup>).

Please note that this value is only accepted when your `pm` value is set to `8` (RADAR).

clt.description: Clutter profile name. If not supplied, but `cll` > `0` then `Minimal.clt` will be used

elevation.description:
Elevation:
* `1` - Digital Surface Model (DSM)
* `2` - Digital Terrain Model (DTM)

buildings.description:
Global OSM buildings layer to enhance DTM:
* `0` - Disabled
* `1` - Enabled

units.description:

* `m_amsl` - Define units in meters and kilometers above mean sea level.
* `f` - Define units in (imperial) feet and miles above ground level.
* `f_amsl` - Define units in (imperial) feet and miles above mean sea level.

col.description:
Colour schema code or a string eg. `RED2BLUE.dBm` of your chosen output colour schema. 

Numerical codes:
* `1` - Cellular (5)
* `2` - Red
* `3` - Green
* `4` - Blue
* `5` - Microwave (7)
* `7` - Custom RGB
* `8` - Automatic by frequency
* `9` - Greyscale/GIS
* `10` - Rainbow (24)
* `11` - Green/Blue/Red
* `13` - Sub noise floor (10)
* `14` - TV broadcasting (4)
* `15` - Red threshold
* `16` - Green threshold
* `17` - Blue threshold

Filename examples: 

* RAINBOW.dBm
* CUSTOMSCHEMA.dBm

Please note that if you have created your own custom colour schema then you can use the name of the schema here.

out.description:

* `6` - Reference Signal Received Power (dBm)

* `9` - Throughput (kbps)

ber.description:
Bit-Error-Rate (These should be combined with an appropriate `mod` value in the `output` object):
* `0` - Not used (default)
* `1` - 0.1 / 10e-1
* `2` - 0.01 / 10e-2
* `3` - 0.001 / 10e-3
* `4` - 0.0001 / 10e-4
* `5` - 0.00001 / 10e-5
* `6` - 0.000001 / 10e-6

LoRa Spread Factors (These are only valid for a LoRa `mod` value (`11`) in the `output` object):

* `9` - LoRa SF9 / 1758bps
* `10` - LoRa SF10 / 977bps
* `11` - LoRa SF11 / 537bps
* `12` - LoRa SF12 / 293bps
